- Windows 7 look: about 180 more pictures from the supplied Windows 7 and Vista icon packs (all 64 x 64, one size) take the place of the thin line icons: arrows, check, plus, cut, bin, star, calendar, printer, home, folders, the media controls and many more. The desktop's own items (This PC, Recycle Bin, Explorer, Paint, Command Prompt, Task Manager, Control Panel, Settings, Store, the games, Notes, Calculator, Voice recorder, Messages ...) and the music and video players (the real Windows Media Player pictures) use them too. The whole Windows 7, Vista and MSN sets are kept in the repository (icon-sources/) for later use.
- Windows 7 File Explorer on the desktop: it opens on Computer, the drives and partitions (Internal storage, Data, System, and any SD card or USB) with a bar of the space used and "X free of Y"; the left pane and the list show the pictures of Documents, Music, Pictures, Videos, Downloads and Camera folders, and of picture, video, music, archive, table, APK, text and document files.
- Task Manager window of the desktop: it has its real pages now - Processes, Performance (the CPU, memory, disk and network graphs), App history, Startup apps, Details, Services - with the slim icon rail on the left in Windows 11 and the tabs along the top in the other looks.
- Messages in the Windows 95, XP and 7 looks is MSN Messenger: the menu bar, the banner with the status, the contact list in Online and Not Online groups with the little green and red people, the "I want to..." panel, and a conversation written as "Name says:" lines. The other looks (Windows 11, 10, Material, AMOLED ...) keep the Messages they had.
- Windows Media Player 12 skin (Music): stop, previous and next are the Windows 7 pictures, and the pressed picture shows while the key is held.
- Windows 11 desktop: the right-click menu is acrylic (the blurred desktop shows through), the window title bar is see-through, and so are the Sort and View menus of File Explorer. File Explorer has Properties for files and folders (General: name, type, location, size, size on disk, what a folder holds, dates, read-only and hidden; Security: owner and the real read, write and run rights; Details: picture, music, video and package facts).
- Widgets: adding a widget on the desktop no longer crashes (the One UI logo of the widget page was a shape drawable). The widget board is new: Pulse's own widgets in groups (clocks, music, notes, calendar, system, photos) with a chip each, other apps' widgets under their app; every card is as wide and as high as its widget really is (wide ones take the whole row, nothing is cropped or stretched); a search; and the board stays open after an add so several can be added in one go.
- Desktop icons sit on a grid by default: 4 x 8 upright and 8 x 4 turned, the columns and rows set in the launcher settings; the free placement is still there when the grid is turned off.
- Settings > Appearance: the groups (mode, background, window material, icons, theme, accent colour, picture, and the Material groups) fold and start closed.
- Files: the menu of a file or folder has cut, copy, paste, rename, delete and archive as one row of icons; the archive icon opens a menu of its own with compress, open, extract, add and the rest of the archive jobs; the other entries are grouped under thin lines.
- Torrents: the working folders (".torrent-...") no longer lie in the Downloads folder: they are kept out of sight in the app's own storage, and a collector removes the ones nobody wants any more (at start, when a download is removed, when one finishes; the ones older versions left in Downloads go too, or are moved when their download is still waiting). The files of one pack download together into the pack's own folder, and a magnet link with no file name reserves a ".mkv" file until the real name is known.
- Keyboard: a new screenshot, camera photo or downloaded picture waits in the right slot of the bar and is pasted from where it is, like a video; it is no longer copied into the clipboard. The clipboard has no limit of 300 items any more; "Limit the number of clipboard items" (off at first) sets one, 3000 when turned on, up to 20000.
- Voice recorder: the record colour follows the look's accent by default (the first dot in the settings; the five fixed colours can still be picked), a long press on a recording picks it (then more can be picked, all selected, and deleted at once, after a question), and the extra look icon at the top is gone (the look is in the settings).
